Resolves #9553

Applications can compose awaited request, response, rejection-recovery and post-parse policies on Pipelines executing in App or Data. Ordinary Neo classes carry behavior; serialized descriptors carry configuration and explicit worker module paths. Realm globals run before local policies, and awaited replacement preserves in-flight handler snapshots until their final use settles.

Request preparation precedes cache lookup. Chain identity and the existing cache-entry fence prevent old policy work from hitting or publishing newer-policy snapshots. Streams remain uncached, transform batches before delivery, and forward rows/progress to the App Pipeline. Intercepted pushes preserve arrival order and publish a failure receipt without poisoning later arrivals.

Evidence: L3 achieved and required — genuine packed-consumer execution in source, ESM, webpack development and webpack production, plus a rendered portal guide. No close-target residuals.

| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | `interceptor.Base`, `Pipeline` and Data's `setPipelineInterceptors` implement the original five requirements plus post-parse hooks; the consumer fixture uses ordinary startup/imports. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: `InterceptorChain.spec` and `PipelineInterceptors.spec` cover readiness, ordering, recovery, replacement, partial construction cleanup, validation before registration and exact-once retirement, including throwing teardown, public clearing and cloneable rejection controls. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: both old-request-preparation and old-post-parse completion races run against a new global chain; cache ownership remains per Pipeline. CI-covered: counted HTTP in all four consumer layouts. |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: real `connection.fire('push')` arrival/error/destruction controls and the existing Pipeline baseline. CI-covered: both realms deliver six ordered batches across two uncached stream reads, with progress and unchanged terminal summaries. |
| AC-5 | CI-covered: `PipelineInterceptorWorkspace.spec.mjs`, four layouts, actual App/Data realm markers and independent HTTP counters. The Engine is npm-packed/extracted; custom classes execute rather than merely appearing in a bundle. |
| AC-6 | Full units; affected consumer/build checks; JSDoc/parse/architecture guards; regenerated class hierarchy; existing data guide and Structural Inventory updated. Portal Mermaid render checked. |

## Deltas from ticket

- Native consumer testing exposed the installed-source Data loader's package-relative app path. It now uses the existing App Worker package-depth convention; compiled loading retains the existing scoped webpack contexts. The broader provisional URL redesign is unchanged.
- Streaming needed prepared headers and a Data-to-App event carrier for transformed batches to be observable. Both are included. Intercepted Data rejections preserve cloneable reasons and use a message-only Error fallback for uncloneable values instead of entering the legacy lost-counterpart retry/null path; the no-interceptor retry controls remain unchanged.
- Failure controls also required shared remote-initialization attempt ownership: failed preload releases every waiter, refuses configured reads before dispatch and validates callable configuration before Pipeline registration.

Change class: `capability`. `agent-preflight` is not hosted in this Engine checkout; local parse, JSDoc, alignment, whitespace, file-size and architectural guards ran; the shared PR baseline validates body/authorship in CI.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: An owner that "attempts every teardown once" has to contain each failure itself. Rethrowing it to whoever released the last lease charges an unrelated operation with another owner's cleanup.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: `RemoteMethodAccess.sendReply` contains a non-cloneable reply only by logging it (#12985). Any remote method that rejects with non-cloneable data therefore leaves its caller unsettled. That debt is inherited, not this PR's; RA-4 keeps the new carrier from routing user-thrown values into it.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: Leasing before readiness, combined with a lazy chain-identity cache fence, keeps policy consistent per operation without a live-Pipeline registry. That shape fits any realm-global policy that is replaced while work is in flight.

<details><summary>Falsifier spec (drop into <code>test/playwright/unit/data/</code>; its <code>reset()</code> writes the statics only because of F3)</summary>

```js
import {setup} from '../../setup.mjs';

setup({appConfig: {name: 'Review20487Falsifier'}});

import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import Neo            from '../../../../src/Neo.mjs';
import * as core      from '../../../../src/core/_export.mjs';
import Connection     from '../../../../src/data/connection/Base.mjs';
import Interceptor    from '../../../../src/data/interceptor/Base.mjs';
import Pipeline       from '../../../../src/data/Pipeline.mjs';
import StreamParser   from '../../../../src/data/parser/Stream.mjs';

const control = {armed: false, gate: null};

class FailingPostParse extends Interceptor {
    static config = {className: 'Test.Review20487.FailingPostParse'}
    postParse() {throw new Error('postParse refused')}
}
FailingPostParse = Neo.setupClass(FailingPostParse);

class Brittle extends Interceptor {
    static config = {className: 'Test.Review20487.Brittle'}
    async request(params) {if (control.gate) await control.gate; return params}
    destroy() {const armed = control.armed; super.destroy(); if (armed) throw new Error('teardown failed')}
}
Brittle = Neo.setupClass(Brittle);

async function reset() {
    control.armed = false;
    control.gate  = null;
    try {await Pipeline.setGlobalInterceptors([])} catch {}
    Pipeline.globalInterceptorChain?.retire?.();
    Pipeline.globalInterceptorChain  = null;
    Pipeline.globalInterceptorChange = null
}

async function create() {
    const pipeline = Neo.create(Pipeline, {connection: {module: Connection, url: '/review'}});
    await Promise.all([pipeline.ready(), pipeline.connection.ready()]);
    pipeline.connection.read = async () => ({ok: true});
    return pipeline
}

const settle = promise => promise.then(value => ({value}), error => ({error: error?.message ?? String(error)}));

async function destroyMidRead(prepare) {
    const pipeline = await create();
    await prepare?.(pipeline);
    let release;
    const gate = new Promise(resolve => release = resolve);
    pipeline.connection.read = async () => {await gate; return {ok: true}};
    const pending = settle(pipeline.read({}));
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10));
    pipeline.destroy();
    release();
    return pending
}

test.describe('Review #20487 falsifiers', () => {
    test.beforeEach(reset);
    test.afterEach(reset);

    test('F1: a retired chain teardown failure must not replace an unrelated in-flight result', async () => {
        await Pipeline.setGlobalInterceptors([{module: Brittle}]);
        const pipeline = await create();
        let release;
        control.gate = new Promise(resolve => release = resolve);
        const inFlight = settle(pipeline.read({}));
        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10));
        control.armed = true;
        await settle(Pipeline.setGlobalInterceptors([]));
        control.gate = null;
        release();
        expect(await inFlight).toEqual({value: {ok: true}});
        pipeline.destroy()
    });

    test('F2: a throwing previous handler must not leave a retired chain installed', async () => {
        await Pipeline.setGlobalInterceptors([{module: Brittle}]);
        const pipeline = await create();
        control.armed = true;
        await settle(Pipeline.setGlobalInterceptors([]));
        control.armed = false;
        expect(await settle(pipeline.read({}))).toEqual({value: {ok: true}});
        pipeline.destroy()
    });

    test('F3: an empty global replacement restores the never-configured read contract', async () => {
        const never = await destroyMidRead();
        await Pipeline.setGlobalInterceptors([{module: Brittle}]);
        await Pipeline.setGlobalInterceptors([]);
        expect(await destroyMidRead()).toEqual(never)
    });

    test('F5: an empty local replacement restores the never-configured read contract', async () => {
        const never   = await destroyMidRead();
        const cleared = await destroyMidRead(async pipeline => {
            await pipeline.setInterceptors([{module: Brittle}]);
            await pipeline.setInterceptors([])
        });
        expect(cleared).toEqual(never)
    });

    test('F4: a post-parse refusal mid-stream releases the still-open response body', async () => {
        let cancelled = null;
        const stream = new ReadableStream({
            start(controller) {controller.enqueue(new TextEncoder().encode('{"id":1}\n{"id":2}\n'))},
            cancel(reason) {cancelled = reason?.message ?? String(reason)}
        });
        const pipeline = Neo.create(Pipeline, {
            connection  : {module: Connection, url: '/review'},
            interceptors: [{module: FailingPostParse}],
            parser      : {module: StreamParser, chunkSize: 1, initialChunkSize: 1}
        });
        await Promise.all([pipeline.ready(), pipeline.connection.ready()]);
        pipeline.connection.read = async () => ({stream, total: 0});
        expect((await settle(pipeline.read({}))).error).toBe('postParse refused');
        expect(cancelled).not.toBeNull();
        pipeline.destroy()
    });
});
```
